Meeting header: 2026-04-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Riya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Cobalt CTO), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Jordan Lee (Infra)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Cobalt's current OpenAI usage, performance pain points, and requirements for Dedicated or Private deployment; determine feasibility and next steps for a pilot.

00:00 Daniel Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Daniel, I'm the AE covering this segment. With me is Riya, our solutions engineer.
00:08 Alex Martinez: Hey Daniel, thanks. I'm Alex, CTO at Cobalt. Priya and Jordan are here.
00:13 Priya Singh: Hi team.
00:15 Jordan Lee: Hey. Sorry, connection a little spotty on my side.
00:20 Daniel Park: No problem. We'll record. Quick agenda: understand your current stack and traffic, pain points with OpenAI, security/compliance requirements, and talk about Dedicated vs Private and a possible benchmark. Does that sound right?
00:30 Alex Martinez: Yeah that's good. We're trying to get off OpenAI for most of our production reasons — cost and latency predictability — but we also want to make sure we don't regress on quality.
00:41 Riya Kapoor: Great. Can you give us a sense of current usage? tokens per month, model flavors, and any self-host attempts?
00:48 Priya Singh: Sure. We're averaging about 1.2B tokens a month across a mix of chat and generation endpoints. Mostly using OpenAI gpt-4o and some gpt-4-turbo variants for chat. We've started experimenting locally with vLLM and TGI for smaller models — mostly for cost-sensitive batch jobs and A/B experiments.
01:05 Alex Martinez: The sticky part is throughput spikes — sale cycles cause 3-4x usage for a few days — so we need predictable autoscaling or burst capacity.
01:15 Daniel Park: Understood. Our Dedicated offering gives reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. We also expose model variants so you can route to cheaper quantized models during spikes.
01:27 Priya Singh: When you say "quantized models", are they compatible with our current prompt engineering? We want eval parity — generate the same outputs within acceptable delta.
01:36 Riya Kapoor: That's a great question. We're focused on model compatibility layers — we host curated open models and provide verified performance profiles. For parity, we run evals using your prompts. The goal is to measure output drift vs OpenAI. For many customers, we hit acceptable parity by tuning temperature, context formatting, and sometimes small adapter layers.
01:55 Jordan Lee: How do you handle inference stack differences — like vLLM optimizations vs your runtime? We rely on KV cache performance for long chat histories.
02:05 Riya Kapoor: Our runtime handles KV cache and continuous batching; we select kernels based on model and sequence length. vLLM and TGI are in the ecosystem — we often validate models converted from those runtimes. There can be quirks: tokenization differences or subtle tokenization offsets sometimes cause different generations. That's why we recommend a benchmark run with your eval set.
02:25 Alex Martinez: Security is a big one — SOC 2, SSO, KMS for encryption. If we go Dedicated, is data encrypted at rest and in transit? Who retains keys?
02:34 Daniel Park: For Hosted we handle keys, for Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. For Private/on-prem we support customer KMS/HSM. We have SOC 2 and ISO docs we can share.
02:46 Priya Singh: If we move to Dedicated, do you let us pin model versions and do canary rollouts? We need deterministic releases across teams.
02:54 Riya Kapoor: Yes — we support version pinning, rollouts, canary/AB, and automatic fallback policies. Rollouts are per-route and per-model.
03:03 Jordan Lee: Network-wise, we have strict IP allowlists and flat VPC with egress restrictions. Private deployment might be necessary. What's involved?
03:12 Daniel Park: Private requires a short implementation plan: control plane still runs in our region, but runtime can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem render — depends on compliance. We'll need a network diagram and a list of allowed ports. Jordan, that matches your ask?
03:24 Jordan Lee: Yeah. We'll share our network topology.
03:26 Alex Martinez: On the quality front — how do you run evals? We have a set of 1k prompts and reference outputs. We need to ensure not just perplexity but business metric parity (conversion, accuracy for classification tasks).
03:37 Riya Kapoor: We run automated eval harnesses and can include behavioral metrics — e.g., conversion proxies — but we'll need your mapping. Typically we run token-level similarity, BLEU-like metrics, and human spot checks for edge cases. We can also run side-by-side benchmarks against OpenAI and a vLLM baseline.
03:56 Priya Singh: Does Redwood support custom tokenizers or do we have to convert models to your stack?
04:02 Riya Kapoor: We support a range of tokenizers and will validate conversions. For models that require custom tokenizers we have a process to integrate them, but that can add to onboarding time.
04:12 Alex Martinez: Cost — can you give rough math? Right now OpenAI is expensive at scale.
04:17 Daniel Park: Sure. If I rough-approx: at 1.2B tokens a month, Hosted costs can be high depending on model. Dedicated moves you to a committed GPU pool; costs drop per token and you get predictable spend. We'll send example committed pricing with a few scenarios: reserved x GPUs, burst buffer, and private pricing.
04:34 Priya Singh: Also curious about latency SLOs. We need p95 < 250ms for short-chat completions. Can Redwood reach that on Dedicated?
04:44 Riya Kapoor: p95 of 250ms depends on model size and sequence length. For optimized models (quantized 8-bit LLMs) on modern GPUs we can hit that for smaller context lengths. For very large models it'll be higher. We can map your actual prompt lengths and target SLO and suggest model profiles.
05:04 Jordan Lee: Do you expose tracing and per-token cost analysis in the console? Our finance team wants granular bills.
05:09 Daniel Park: Yes — Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and trace hooks. You can export billing and integrate with cost monitoring.
05:18 Alex Martinez: A couple of edge questions: we run some batch jobs on TGI for long-running transformations. Will those run on Dedicated?
05:26 Riya Kapoor: Yes, batch jobs are supported. We also provide autoscaling policies specific for batch vs low-latency jobs. TGI compatibility depends on model format; we validate conversions.
05:36 Priya Singh: We also experiment with vLLM on our internal infra because of lower latency on multi-GPU sharded setups — any gotchas moving that workload to Redwood?
05:45 Riya Kapoor: vLLM's sharding strategies can differ; our runtime focuses on kernel selection and balanced scheduling. If you need the same sharded topo, Private on-prem is probably the closest parity. For Dedicated we can do optimized multi-GPU pools but we may recommend model quantization or sequence-length optimizations to hit latency targets.
06:06 Alex Martinez: Let's talk rollback/fallbacks. If we push a model and it underperforms vs OpenAI, can we route back automatically?
06:14 Riya Kapoor: Yes, we have automatic fallback policies. You can configure per-route policy to fall back to Hosted OpenAI (if you'd keep that) or to a different model variant. We also do canary metrics so you can detect regressions early.
06:28 Jordan Lee: What about data residency? We have EU users and some data cannot leave region.
06:33 Daniel Park: We have region controls on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have region options, but if you need strict residency then Private in your region or on-prem is recommended.
06:44 Priya Singh: Operationally, how long to onboard to Dedicated and run an eval?
06:48 Daniel Park: Typically 2-4 weeks for a pilot: provisioning a small Dedicated pool, onboarding models, running evals, and a short production test. Private/on-prem adds a few weeks for network/setup. Riya, anything to add?
06:58 Riya Kapoor: We'll also prepare a benchmark plan split into unit tests (latency, throughput) and eval parity checks. We'll need your 1k prompt set and access logs.
07:08 Alex Martinez: OK. For success criteria: 1) cost reduction vs OpenAI by at least 35% for same traffic, 2) no regression in top-3 business metrics, 3) secure key management and SOC2 compliance.
07:22 Daniel Park: That helps. We'll map those into the pilot scope.
07:25 Priya Singh: One last technical nit: do you support padded batching or mixed precision to reduce cost?
07:30 Riya Kapoor: Yes — our runtime supports continuous batching, mixed precision, and dynamic kernel selection. We also have caching for common prefixes which often helps chat workloads.
07:42 Jordan Lee: If we do Private, are logs still accessible to Redwood? We need audit logs but no PII export.
07:48 Daniel Park: In Private you control logs; we can forward audit hooks to your SIEM. We also support redaction and log retention policies.
07:57 Alex Martinez: Great. Let's summarize next steps.
08:00 Daniel Park: Next steps: I'll send committed Dedicated pricing and the SOC2 pack. Riya will draft the benchmark plan. You'll share usage logs and the eval set. We'll schedule the tech deep-dive on 2026-04-07. Any additions?
08:16 Priya Singh: Please include vLLM/TGI conversion notes and sample commands for converting tokens.
08:21 Riya Kapoor: Will do.
08:23 Jordan Lee: I'll send the network diagram.
08:25 Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the benchmark.
08:28 Daniel Park: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
